observed_text: Optical penetration depth in continuous Ag/Al in the visible is about 10–20 nm.
implied_text: A continuous metal stack of that depth (~40–85 atomic planes) is the minimum connected buffer for a stable collective reflected beam.
description: Reflection requires a connected electron-gas volume on the order of the optical penetration depth; fewer planes starve the collective screening response.
notes: Plane count derived from (111) spacing; the measured quantity is the nanometre threshold.

observed_text: Below roughly 5–10 nm of continuous film, reflectivity collapses and transmission rises. Islanded films fail at any nominal thickness.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning or a disconnected morphology starves the buffer and the mirror disappears.
description: The mirror dies when the connected node count falls below a few-nanometre continuity / penetration cliff.
notes: Percolation vs electromagnetic penetration are two routes to the same failure class.

observed_text: Al ħωp ≈ 15 eV and Ag ħωp ≈ 9 eV give plasma periods ~0.3–0.5 fs. Single-electron streaking is attosecond.
implied_text: Collective screening and the phase-reversed re-radiation complete on the plasma-period timescale.
description: The electron population must finish the reflection cycle in a few 10^-16 to 10^-15 s; the image is already complete on any macroscopic clock.

observed_text: Metals transmit when the drive exceeds the plasma (Al, alkalis) or the interband-shifted optical edge (Ag ~3.9 eV).
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock → the population cannot finish a cycle in one period → transmission.
description: The same machine that fails by buffer starvation at low thickness fails by clock overrun above the plasma / interband edge.
value_text: ω > ωp (Al ~15 eV; Ag optical edge ~3.9 eV)
notes: Cross-cite plasma-frequency-cutoff, which owns this collapse as its primary artifact. value_si is Al ωp/2π order of magnitude.

observed_text: Operating window is ω < ωp (or Ag’s interband edge) plus a continuous film at least one penetration depth thick.
implied_text: This is a driven collective response, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a latched state.
description: Reflection has an operating threshold on drive frequency and thickness, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Polished Ag reflects ≳95% in most of the visible; Al ~90%. No continuous external power to the metal beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Stable phase-reversed reflected beam with material-typical R(λ), at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a macroscopic reflected beam without a hold-power budget.

observed_text: No continuous external power is required to maintain the reflected image beyond the incident field itself.
implied_text: Hold-power of the mirror is zero; the drive is the light being reflected.
description: The mirror is not a powered lamp. Continuous draw to hold R is zero.

observed_text: The penetration depth is δ = λ/4πk, and k is itself an emergent optical constant of the same electrons.
implied_text: QSA currently takes the measured penetration depth as the buffer specification; it does not derive that depth from a more primitive node count.
description: The spatial buffer is located but not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³. KV = 25 kT at 300 K gives V = 2.1–2.4e-26 m³: a sphere 3.4–3.6 nm across or a cube 2.8–2.9 nm on a side. The single-domain diameter is about 200–300 nm.
implied_text: The smallest grain that holds its direction at room temperature on laboratory time is a few nanometres across. Real magnets sit two orders of magnitude above that, so thermal erasure of whole grains is not what limits them. Soft matrices lack the barrier.
description: The thermal-stability size of the latch cell is a few nanometres for Nd2Fe14B. It depends on the waiting time chosen and is not a cliff.
value_text: V ≈ 2.1–2.4e-26 m³ (3.4–3.6 nm sphere); KV = 25 kT
notes: The first version called this volume ~30 nm; a 30 nm cube is about 29 000 kT. 25 kT is the convention for a 100 s measurement. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: A usable motor force is F = ∇(m·B) from a large aligned population. There is no universal millimetre-scale cliff.
implied_text: Macroscopic force is synchronized output of many latched grains. Force scales with aligned moment; the sharp cliff stays at the grain.
description: The sample envelope is a capacity, not a second spatial cliff. No single minimum N for a usable force is extracted.
value_text: force scales with aligned m; no universal N

observed_text: Free-electron gyromagnetic ratio γe/2π = 28 024.951 MHz/T (CODATA 2022).
implied_text: Baseline single-spin clock of the latch. Write/erase of a hard magnet is set by field sweep and wall motion, not this carrier.
description: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession clock; holding the state does not require running that clock as a power draw.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B anisotropy K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³ at room temperature (4.30 on single crystals, 4.9 in another tabulation); per-grain barrier ΔE ≈ K1V. A real magnet reverses at 16–18 % of the anisotropy field. Holding costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Anisotropy holds the grain's moment along an axis. Exchange, a separate resource, makes the grain one moment. Energy is spent only on write/erase.
description: The latch exists because a barrier protects orientation at zero hold-power.
notes: Barrier energy is K1V, not K1 alone. The first version used 4.5 MJ/m³, which is inside the range but was not found in an opened source. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B Curie temperature 585–588 K; commercial grades list 310–380 °C. Iron has a hundredth of the anisotropy and a Curie temperature of 1043 K.
implied_text: Loss of exchange order at Tc removes the moment itself. The Curie temperature is set by exchange, not by kT exceeding the anisotropy barrier.
description: Thermal loss of magnetic order at the Curie point, an exchange threshold.
notes: The first version attributed this collapse to the anisotropy barrier.

observed_text: τ = τ0 exp(KV/kT). KV = 25 kT (100 s with τ0 = 1e-9 s) at 300 K is a 3.4–3.6 nm sphere for Nd2Fe14B.
implied_text: Same barrier, smaller volume: the retention time falls exponentially. There is no critical size.
description: Small grains lose their direction thermally without reaching Tc; the size quoted depends on the waiting time.
value_text: KV ≈ 25 kT (≈3.5 nm sphere, Nd2Fe14B, 100 s)
notes: Primary owner of this crossover is superparamagnetism. The comparison with a thin-film mirror in the first version is withdrawn.

observed_text: A transverse shock of 22.3 GPa turns Nd2Fe14B into a weak magnet; 6.26–7.16 GPa demagnetizes sintered magnets by intergranular fracture, recoverable by annealing. Hydrogen decrepitation gives a demagnetized hydrided powder.
implied_text: Shock and chemical breakdown remove remanence without reaching Tc, through fracture, a pressure-induced change of magnetic phase, or a change of material.
description: Shock and hydrogen decrepitation erase a hard magnet below its Curie point.
notes: Two measured shock points, no threshold established. No source was found for plastic deformation, which the first version listed.

observed_text: A static magnet at rest produces no continuous I²R or hysteresis heat.
implied_text: Stable directional moment and static field/force at zero continuous power, inside the Tc / KV / lattice envelope.
description: Holding the latched state costs zero watts. Energy is the write/erase loop area only.

observed_text: The first sintered magnet had coercivity 960 kA/m (about 1.2 T), 16–18 % of the 6.7–7.65 T anisotropy field. In simulation a defect-free cubic grain reaches 3.94 T against an ideal 6.09 T, about 65 %.
implied_text: QSA does not have a buffer/barrier specification for the mesoscale write threshold (nucleation, grain boundaries, dipolar coupling).
description: Coercivity is a mesoscale quantity the mapping does not specify. With the stability size two orders below the single-domain size, this step, not KV, limits a real magnet.

observed_text: A single conversion event is already the microscopic effect. Photoemission persists from atomically thin or adsorbate-covered emitters once hν clears φ.
implied_text: No collective buffer is required. One electron at a surface is the hardware. Escape depth limits collection, not the on/off of the gate.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack.
notes: How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer.

observed_text: Streaking delays of tens to hundreds of attoseconds. Intensity sets rate, not one-event latency.
implied_text: The conversion is finished on any optical-cycle-averaged laboratory clock.
description: Single-electron conversion latency sits in the attosecond regime.

observed_text: Typical φ 2–6 eV (Cs low, Pt high). KE = hν − φ above threshold.
implied_text: φ is the load-bearing gate. Below it (linear regime) conversion does not occur. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
description: The photoelectric effect is a single-particle energy gate at the work function.
notes: value_si is ~4 eV in joules, mid-class.

observed_text: hν < φ → no linear photoemission (only a Fowler tail exponential in (φ−hν)/kT).
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below the work function the gate stays shut.

observed_text: A material- and face-typical φ, zero photocurrent below it, linear Kmax(ν) above it.
implied_text: The stable output is the threshold itself plus the above-threshold kinetic-energy line.
description: The machine’s stable product is a work-function gate and a linear surplus-energy line.

observed_text: Face dependence and contamination shift φ by tenths of an eV. QSA takes measured φ as the gate.
implied_text: No derivation of the 2–6 eV class from a surface-dipole plus chemical-potential construction.
description: The gate is located and shown to be a surface resource; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: Do not identify φ with Ag’s 3.9 eV optical plasma edge.
